literal: Being poured even having seen, poison having consumed they will be calm, esteem-worthy graciousness those who desire.
translation: Those who desire highly esteemed graciousness will calmly drink poison, even when they see it being poured for them.
modern: எல்லாராலும் விரும்பத்தக்க சிறந்த நாகரிகத்தை விரும்புபவர்கள், தமக்கு நஞ்சை ஊற்றுவதைப் பார்த்தாலும், அதனை உண்டு அமைதியாக இருப்பார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet illustrates the extreme extent of graciousness and benignity. It says that those who value noble, esteemed social conduct will accept even poison from others without causing a scene. By drinking the poison calmly, they prioritize the feelings and dignity of the person serving it over their own lives. The word 'நாகரிகம்' (urbanity or graciousness) here denotes a profound, self-sacrificing courtesy that refuses to embarrass another person.
